# phase-103 — Add structured logging so programs stop printing to stdout

## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
A program that wants to record what it did has say and console.log and nothing else. There is no level, no destination other than the console, no timestamp attached to a log line, and no way to turn logging off. So a library cannot log without polluting the output of the program using it, and a program that wants diagnostics has to print them where its real output goes - which means a user cannot silence them without editing the source. This is why every Redblue program that has ever needed diagnostics has used a conditional and hoped for the best.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Add a logging facility with levels, a settable threshold, a settable destination, and a timestamp on each record, so a library can log without speaking to stdout. Make the default level quiet enough that adding a log call cannot change a program's observable output, since a library that changes its caller's output is a defect. Decide whether timestamps make records non-deterministic, and if so keep them out of anything a test would compare - the corpus compares output literally, so a timestamp in the default path would break it.

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] a record at or above the threshold is emitted and one below it is not, asserted by capturing the destination, for every adjacent pair of levels
- [ ] the default level emits nothing, so adding a log call to a library cannot change a program's observable output - asserted by a corpus-style golden comparison
- [ ] the destination is settable to a file and a record written there is readable back with the level and message intact
- [ ] a timestamp is present on each record and a test proves a deterministic mode exists that omits it, so corpus goldens stay stable
- [ ] logging to a closed or unwritable destination raises a catchable error rather than aborting the program
- [ ] the tree-walker and the bytecode VM emit equal records, compared as data across both engines
- [ ] SPEC.md documents the levels, the default, and the determinism stance
- [ ] edge_* tests cover the threshold at its extremes, a record with an empty message, a multi-line message, and concurrent-ish interleaved writes from nested calls
